title: Treat unparseable YAML shapes same as templates: taint entire container
context: The scanner silently dropped lines it couldn't parse (quoted keys, merge keys) from label/selector maps. Dropping keys makes selectors MORE permissive, not less, creating false-positive edges between resources that don't actually match. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Generalized the 'blockTemplated' taint mechanism to 'unresolvedContainers': any line KEY_LINE can't parse now marks its parent container as unresolved (null), not silently skipped. This treats template injection and unparseable YAML as equivalent failure modes: incomplete knowledge of a container's contents disqualifies it from matching.
consequences: No false-positive selector/label edges from quoted keys or YAML merge keys
Windows CRLF line endings now work (combined with regex fix)
Simpler model: 'unresolved' has one meaning, not two parallel code paths
ReplicaSet now wired into pod-spec and labels tables for completeness
alternatives_rejected: Extend KEY_LINE regex to match quoted keys — but new YAML shapes would still slip through silently
Continue silently dropping unparseable lines — already proven to create false positives
Error on any unparseable line — too strict for valid YAML the scanner doesn't handle
Keep separate mechanisms for templates vs. unrecognized lines — parallel logic hides bugs
